title: POWER and ^ return #NUM! for 0^0, allow negative bases when 1/y rounds to an odd 32-bit integer to 15 digits, and double-round 10^126
statement: In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, POWER(0,0) and 0^0 return #NUM! and POWER(0,-1) returns #DIV/0!. For a negative base with fractional exponent y, Excel accepts the real root -POWER(|x|, y) when 1/y rounded to 15 significant decimal digits is an odd signed 32-bit integer ((-8)^(1/3) = -1.9999999999999998, (-32)^(1/5) = -2, while (-8)^(2/3) = #NUM!). Integer exponents use staged binary exponentiation and flush subnormals to +0 (2^-1074 = 0), while POWER(10, k) double-rounds 10^k through 64-bit significand precision, giving 0x5a17a2ecc414a040 at k = 126 (1 ULP above nearest ...a03f).
basis: Measured across all 59 rows of f1_power in Excel 16.0.20527.20088, Excel 16.0.20527 POWER(10, 0..308) sweeps, and 62,635 of 62,635 full-bank POWER witness rows.
